_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.

items.text: NEW: typing a word in the merge sidebar's Search box now surfaces EVERY course with that word in the title (it used to miss some — your 'First Course in Russian' case). And the old 'Match the CCR table filters' checkbox is gone: the worklist is no longer tied to the main table's filters — use the sidebar's own Search + Discipline + Beg/Int/Adv controls instead. Flag anything a keyword still misses (give me the exact course/ID) and I'll dig into that one row.

NEW: to just RENAME one course (no merge) — e.g. 'Russian 1' → 'Russian (Beg)' — open it in the sidebar, leave only that one course checked, edit the Proposed title, and the button flips from 'Confirm merge' to '✓ Save'. It saves the new name to that one course (no merge). Works from the per-row ⚇ Merge too (where you can also change its discipline).

NEW: ‹ › Prev/Next buttons now sit at the TOP of the sidebar next to the 'N of M' counter, so you can step BACKWARD through the queue without scrolling down to the bottom pager. Say if you'd like them somewhere else.

Carry-over from S70 (still worth doing): the worklist groups WORD VARIANTS — 'Conversational Japanese' ↔ 'Japanese Conversation', 'Assisting' ↔ 'Assistant' (~866 more group). Confirm the clean language-conversation families when you get a chance. Where a group shows an amber '⚠ Spans N disciplines' note, eyeball it for homonyms (music vs office 'keyboard') before confirming.

Course levels show a Beg / Int / Adv chip and the Levels filter reads Beg · Int · Adv · Lab · WkExp. It classifies by Title-5 §55050 — explicit ranges (1-2/3-4/5-6) and words/ordinals are reliable; a bare single number ('Spanish 3') is just a HINT you can override. Eyeball a language or ESL family and correct any level that reads wrong.
Standing bonus: we'll keep adding Arroyo-Seco-style California plein-air landscapes (Redmond, Guy Rose, Wendt, Payne) to First Light — flag any artist/work you'd love and we'll source it.
